answers.quote: Do you know who came first and explored our India? It was the Portuguese.
answers.notes: Portuguese first per c02

answers.quote: It was Vasco da Gama who landed in Calicut in India on May 17, 1498.
answers.notes: Date May 17, 1498 per c03

answers.answer: উত্তমাশা অন্তরীপ (Cape of Good Hope) ঘুরে সরাসরি সমুদ্রপথে
answers.quote: The discovery of direct maritime route to Asia round the Cape of Good Hope by the Portuguese under Vasco da Gama in 1498 marked the beginning of a new era in the history of Euro-Asian trade.
answers.notes: Direct route round Cape of Good Hope per c05

answers.answer: মশলার জন্য সরাসরি সমুদ্রপথ খোঁজা ও খ্রিস্টধর্ম প্রচার
answers.quote: The original idea of sending the Portuguese that was of the Pope to find the direct sea routes to the resource rich countries especially for the spices and promote Christianity.
answers.notes: Pope's idea: sea routes for spices + promote Christianity per c04

answers.answer: বস্ত্র, কাঁচা রেশম ও শোরার (saltpetre) মতো ভারতীয় পণ্যের বিদেশি চাহিদা ছিল
answers.quote: textiles, raw silk and saltpetre were the principal items exported by the Companies
answers.notes: not covered by claims: claims list textiles/raw silk/saltpetre as principal Company exports (c32) but do not state pre-European Indian Ocean trade composition; this is the best supported option

answers.answer: ১৫০০ সালে ভারতীয় সামুদ্রিক ইতিহাসে কোনো 'ভাস্কো দা গামা যুগ' শুরু হয়নি
answers.quote: there was no Vasco da Gama epoch in Indian maritime history that was inaugurated in 1500
answers.notes: Das Gupta: no Vasco da Gama epoch inaugurated in 1500 per c20

answers.quote: In 1510, Alfonzo de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur and made it the capital of the Portuguese eastern empire.
answers.notes: Goa captured from Sultan of Bijapur per c08

answers.quote: In 1510, Alfonzo de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur and made it the capital of the Portuguese eastern empire.
answers.notes: Goa made capital of Portuguese eastern empire per c08

answers.answer: কিলওয়া, আঞ্জাদিব, কান্নানুর ও কোচিনে দুর্গ নির্মাণ
answers.quote: At the beginning of 1505 Francisco d'Almeida set out in command of a large fleet and 1500 soldiers, with orders to build fortresses at Kilwa, Anjadiva, Kannanur and Cochin.
answers.notes: Orders to build fortresses at Kilwa, Anjadiva, Kannanur, Cochin per c07

answers.answer: মালাক্কা দক্ষিণ-পূর্ব এশিয়ার প্রধান বাণিজ্যকেন্দ্র (entrepot) হিসেবে এলাকার সমুদ্রপথ নিয়ন্ত্রণ করত
answers.quote: followed by the occupation of Malacca (1511) which was extremely important as an entreport in Southeast Asia and which controlled the sea-routes in the area.
answers.notes: Malacca entrepot controlling sea-routes per c10

answers.quote: In 1515 the important port of Hormuz at the mouth of the Persian Gulf was conquered
answers.notes: Hormuz conquered in 1515 per c11

answers.answer: এই দখলের মধ্য দিয়েই ভারত মহাসাগরে ভবিষ্যৎ পর্তুগিজ সামুদ্রিক সাম্রাজ্যের ভিত্তি সত্যিকারে স্থাপিত হয়
answers.quote: However, it was not until the capture of Goa from the Bijapur Sultan by Albuquerque in 1510 that the foundation of the future Portuguese maritime empire in the Indian Ocean region was truly laid.
answers.notes: Goa capture truly laid foundation of maritime empire per c09

answers.quote: Under the cartaz system, every Asian ship was required to take a cartaz from the Portuguese. It authorised the vessel to embark on a specified trip.
answers.notes: Cartaz = pass authorising specified trip per c14

answers.quote: If a ship was found without a cartaz, it was automatically confiscated
answers.notes: Ship without cartaz automatically confiscated per c15

answers.answer: নিজেদের জন্য একচেটিয়া বাণিজ্য, এশীয়দের জন্য কার্তাজ-ভিত্তিক লাইসেন্সপ্রাপ্ত বাণিজ্য
answers.quote: The Portuguese system of commerce depended very much on the notion of monopoly trade for the Lusitanians and licensed (cartaz-based) trade for the Asians.
answers.notes: Monopoly for Portuguese, licensed cartaz trade for Asians per c17

answers.quote: In the second half of the 16th century, the Portuguese introduced the so-called qafila or caravan system in the western coast of India.
answers.notes: Qafila/caravan system, second half of 16th c., west coast per c16

answers.quote: pepper was the raison d’être of the Portuguese-Asian trade in the beginning, accounting for in the first two decades of the 16th century as much as 95 per cent of the total Asian cargo
answers.notes: Pepper 95% of Asian cargo in first two decades of 16th c. per c18

answers.answer: ইউরোপে মশলা সরবরাহে একচেটিয়া আধিপত্য এবং বলপ্রয়োগে এশীয় বাণিজ্য নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও কর আদায়
answers.quote: The general purpose of the Portuguese was two-fold: i) to try and monopolize the supply of spices to Europe, and ii) to control and tax Asian trade by force.
answers.notes: Two-fold purpose per c06

answers.quote: The Dutch East India Company was created in 1602 by the merger of several companies
answers.notes: Dutch EIC created 1602 per c24; also c22

answers.quote: In 1605, Admiral Van der Hagen established the first Dutch factory in Masulipattanam in Andhra Pradesh.
answers.notes: First Dutch factory Masulipatnam 1605 per c26

answers.quote: The Dutch negotiated with the king of Chandragiri in 1610 and had another factory at Pulicat and it was fortified and named as Geldria.
answers.notes: Pulicat fortified and named Geldria per c27

answers.quote: In 1627 Dutch Bengal was established.
answers.notes: Dutch Bengal established 1627 per c28

answers.quote: Trivancore Marthanda Varma gave a fatal blow to the Dutch East India Company in the battle of Colachel in 1741, which resulted in complete defeat of Dutch power in Malabar.
answers.notes: Marthanda Varma defeated Dutch at Colachel 1741 per c29

answers.quote: The Dutch East India Company was created in 1602 by the merger of several companies
answers.notes: Created by merger of several companies per c24

answers.quote: The English East India Company was established in 1600 CE as a joint stock company with a monopoly on trade with the East Indies that was guaranteed by a monarch.
answers.notes: English EIC established 1600 per c23

answers.quote: the British East India Company established its presence in India way back in 1612, wherein they established factories in India for trading
answers.notes: British EIC presence/factories in 1612 per c30

answers.answer: রাজা/রানির দেওয়া সনদে পূর্বদেশীয় বাণিজ্যে একচেটিয়া অধিকারসহ যৌথ-মূলধনি কোম্পানি
answers.quote: The English East India Company was established in 1600 CE as a joint stock company with a monopoly on trade with the East Indies that was guaranteed by a monarch.
answers.notes: Joint stock company with monopoly guaranteed by monarch per c23

answers.quote: India was central to the English Company trade throughout accounting for 95 per cent and 84 per cent of the total imports during the latter half of the 17th century.
answers.notes: India 95% and 84% of total imports, latter half 17th c. per c51

answers.answer: ইংরেজরা প্রধানত বস্ত্রে, ওলন্দাজরা প্রধানত মশলায়
answers.quote: The English East India Company mostly traded in cloth and fabric. Meanwhile, the Dutch East India Company dealt largely with the trade of spices.
answers.notes: English cloth/fabric, Dutch spices per c48

answers.quote: both the Dutch and the English established their factories or trading posts in Bengal in the early 1650s, incidentally both in Hughli, the premier port of Bengal in the 17th century.
answers.notes: Both at Hughli in early 1650s per c31

answers.quote: In 1664 Jean-Baptiste Colbert founded the French East India Company
answers.notes: Colbert founded French EIC in 1664 per c35

answers.quote: The company established its first factory at Surat under Francis Caron in 1668 and the Second factory was established a year later in Masulipattanam.
answers.notes: First factory Surat under Francis Caron 1668 per c36

answers.quote: French East India Company under Francois Martin in 1674 established a trading centre at Pondicherry.
answers.notes: Francois Martin, Pondicherry 1674 per c37

answers.quote: In 1701 Pondicherry was made the capital of French settlements in India.
answers.notes: Pondicherry capital in 1701 per c39

answers.quote: The French acquired Mahe in 1720, Yanam in 1731, and Karaikal in 1738.
answers.notes: Mahe 1720, Yanam 1731, Karaikal 1738 per c38

answers.answer: তিনি ১৭৪২ সালে ভারতে ফরাসি সাম্রাজ্যের দায়িত্ব নেন এবং ১৭৪৬ সালে মাদ্রাজ দখল করেন
answers.quote: Later in 1742, Joseph Francois Dupleix took charge of the French empire in India. In 1746 he captured Madras
answers.notes: Dupleix took charge 1742, captured Madras 1746 per c40

answers.answer: ফরাসি বাহিনী পরাজিত হয় এবং ১৭৬১ সালে তাদের রাজধানী পণ্ডিচেরি দখল হয়; ১৭৬৫ সালে শান্তিচুক্তিতে পণ্ডিচেরি ফরাসিদের ফেরত দেওয়া হয়
answers.quote: During the Seven Years War (1756-63) between France and England, the French forces were defeated and the capital was captured in 1761.
answers.notes: French defeated, capital captured 1761 per c41; return in 1765 per c42

answers.quote: The Danish Company had its fort and factory at Tranquebar
answers.notes: Danish fort and factory at Tranquebar per c46

answers.quote: It was Vasco da Gama who landed in Calicut in India on May 17, 1498.
answers.notes: Both true: Portuguese first (c02) and Vasco at Calicut 1498 (c03)

answers.quote: First off the mark in 1600 was the English joint-stock East India Company (EEIC). It was followed two years later by the Dutch East India Company, the Verenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC).
answers.notes: English 1600 first, Dutch two years later per c22, so statement 2 false

answers.quote: followed by the occupation of Malacca (1511) which was extremely important as an entreport in Southeast Asia and which controlled the sea-routes in the area.
answers.notes: Chronology: Vasco 1498 (c03), Goa 1510 (c08), Malacca 1511 (c10), Hormuz 1515 (c11)

answers.quote: In 1664 Jean-Baptiste Colbert founded the French East India Company
answers.notes: Colbert-1664 (c35), Caron-Surat 1668 (c36), Martin-Pondicherry 1674 (c37), Dupleix-Madras 1746 (c40)

answers.answer: A ও R দুটোই সঠিক এবং R, A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: the main challenges came when these nation-states (Dutch, French and English) organized their merchants into chartered companies in the beginning of the 17th century to rival the royal monopoly that was dominated by the Portuguese in the 16th century.
answers.notes: Chartered companies to rival Portuguese royal monopoly per c21; R explains A

answers.quote: Under the cartaz system, every Asian ship was required to take a cartaz from the Portuguese. It authorised the vessel to embark on a specified trip.
answers.notes: Cartaz pair per c14, Geldria pair per c27; qafila as caravan/group system per c16 supports pair 2, wording of escort detail not verbatim in claims

answers.answer: ভারতীয় পণ্যের বিনিময়ে কোম্পানিগুলি প্রধানত রুপোসহ মূল্যবান ধাতু আনত
answers.quote: precious metals, mainly silver, were being exchanged for manufactures and primary goods exported from India. This “bullion for goods” character was the principal feature of the Indo-European trade
answers.notes: Bullion for goods: precious metals mainly silver exchanged for Indian goods per c33
